override.reason: The composite key expression sid + sr.BINDING_KEY_SEP + payload['agent_id'] is repeated in eight new tests rather than factored into a helper that calls sr.binding_key(). Deduplicating it through the function under test would make each assertion tautological -- the test would compute its expectation with the code it is testing and would pass in a world where binding_key composed any key at all. Restating the format independently in the test is the point, not an oversight. In production code the format is NOT duplicated: grep over scripts/ finds exactly one composition site (spine_rail.py:184) and one prefix site (203).

override.reason: The per-agent identity is carried as a '#'-joined string rather than a (session_id, agent_id) pair. That is the classic primitive, and here it is forced: the value is the outer key of a JSON object persisted to .agent-work/.spine-rail-binding.json, so it must serialize as a string. The primitive does not leak either -- binding_key is the single composer and session_view is the single reader of the format, both verified by grep, so a key type object would be a second seam with one implementer.

override.reason: Knowledge of the binding store's key shape now sits in two files: spine_rail.py composes and merges it, while gauge_writer_hook.py:159 still reads binding.get(session_id) directly. The unreachable-today branch (agent_id present as null) is a fail-closed guard, not an unused abstraction; the implementer surfaced it as a decision candidate rather than building for a hypothesis. No unused parameter, hook, or extension point is introduced.

override.reason: binding_key carries a 35-line docstring over a 15-line body, and the release branch carries a 12-line comment. On raw ratio that reads as deodorant. It is not: the prose states WHY (an unusable agent_id must not fall back to the bare key because that files the subagent's entry under the parent's key and silences the parent's gauge) and records the key/sid asymmetry that a future maintainer would otherwise 'fix' into a bug. The repo has no architecture map, so the code site is the only place this decision can live, and the file already documents #202/#261 the same way. The comments explain intent the code cannot express, not code the reader cannot follow.
